title: Lull-to-Lift Launch Scorecard and Comm Folio (May 2026 draft)
content:
Purpose:
A compact, operational playpad for the planned Lull-to-Lift micro-launch. This doc is an actionable scorecard (hour-by-hour) + comm folio for ops during the 24h window. Not final — use as working checklist and update in real time.

TL;DR (one paragraph):
We will ramp a new routing heuristic for model routing (route-v2) starting at 04:00 UTC on 2026-05-22. Traffic will be lifted from 0% -> 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 60% -> 100% across ~6 hours with automated telemetry gates. Primary risks: latency bump in regional EU nodes, cache warmup causing token-cost variance, and a small repro of a reorder bug in session affinity. If gates fail, fall back to route-v1 and initiate rollback.

Primary channels and stakeholders:
- Slack: #release-orchestra (primary), #infra-oncall (pager), #sre-runbook
- Pager: oncall-sre (Marcus Chen)
- Exec updates: send cadence to #exec-ops at 1h, 4h, and postmortem

Hour-by-hour plan (local timestamps relative to 04:00 UTC start):
- T-48h: Final smoke test in staging (responsible: QA, Liam)
- T-24h: Release notes posted to Confluence + customer comm draft (Aisha)
- T-6h: Preflight signoff (all leads): services green, infra capacity reserved, canary infra warmed
- T-1h: Quiet window begins (no unrelated deploys)
- 04:00 UTC (0m): Enable route-v2 at 0% (control path only) — smoke probe + canary logs
- 04:15 (15m): Checkpoint 1: health metrics stable for 15m -> expand to 1%
- 04:45 (45m): Checkpoint 2: 1% sustained 30m -> expand to 5%
- 05:30 (90m): Checkpoint 3: 5% sustained 45m & latency P95 within threshold -> expand to 25%
- 07:00 (180m): Checkpoint 4: 25% sustained 60m -> expand to 60%
- 09:00 (300m): Checkpoint 5: 60% sustained 90m -> expand to 100%
- 12:00 (480m): Soft-stabilization window ends; begin sampling for regression testing and cost telemetry

Staffing matrix (recommended):
- Release lead: Aisha Patel (coord, comms)
- SRE oncall: Marcus Chen (pager)
- Serving runtime lead: Sofia Gutierrez (rollout mechanics)
- QA & E2E: Liam O'Connor (smoke, canary checks)
- Console/Observability: 1 engineer (alerts & dashboards)
- Backup rota: two engineers cross-trained to run rollback steps

Preflight checklist (must all be green before T-1h):
- [ ] Infra capacity reserved (quota + GPU pools)
- [ ] Canary instances pre-warmed with model weights
- [ ] KV/prefix cache prefill heuristics validated in staging
- [ ] Telemetry dashboards deployed and verified (latency, errors, token cost)
- [ ] Canary log sinks connected to retention pipeline
- [ ] Runbook pinned in Slack and SRE pager roster verified
- [ ] Rollback playbook validated in dry-run (no actual traffic)

Go/No-Go gating rules (automated + manual override):
Automated gate (at each step) requires:
- Latency: P95 < 220ms (global) AND regional P95 delta < +20% from baseline
- Error rate: request error rate < 0.5% absolute and < 3x baseline
- Token cost variance: < 15% relative deviation for 30m window
- Resource pressure: GPU saturation < 75%
If any automated gate fails, system auto-holds at current traffic and fires a page to oncall-sre. Release lead makes manual decision with SRE within 15m.

Rollback heuristics (fast path):
- Trigger: sustained P95 > 300ms for 15m OR error rate > 1% for 10m OR region-specific service degradation observed
- Fast rollback action: revert routing config to route-v1 (immutable tag), scale down route-v2 instances, and mark incident channel.
- Communication: immediate Slack post in #release-orchestra and update exec at the 1h checkpoint.

Telemetry gating specifics (dashboards & alerts):
- Dashboards: release/lull-to-lift/overview, release/lull-to-lift/region-EU, release/lull-to-lift/cost-sampler
- Key metrics: p95 latency, p50 latency, error rate (4xx/5xx), retries, req/sec, GPU utilization, tokens-per-request median
- Sampling: randomly sample 1 in 1000 requests for full payload logging; ramp to 1 in 100 after 60% traffic to validate edge cases

Release notes draft (to be posted T-24h as customer-facing snippet):
Title: "Model routing improvements: reduced cold-starts and smarter failover (route-v2)"
Summary: Route-v2 improves prefix affinity and cache reuse, lowering token cost for multi-turn sessions and reducing tail latency for bursty workloads. We expect minimal user visible change; some customers may see transient cost variance during initial ramp.
Notes for engineers:
- Deploy includes a routing config switch and a sidecar process to reconcile session affinity.
- Feature flag: feature/routing/route-v2 (can be toggled per-region)
Known issues (do not hide):
- Small repro of session-reorder seen in test matrix; risk limited to low-traffic sessions and mitigated by affinity TTL reduction.
- EU region extra latency risk under high concurrency (mitigation: pre-warm caches and throttle client bursts).

Post-launch checklist (first 24h):
- [ ] 1h post: short summary + any anomalies to #exec-ops
- [ ] 4h post: handoff to steady-state owners + add changelog entry
- [ ] 24h post: consolidate telemetry, begin targeted regressions against golden prompt set
- [ ] 72h post: final postmortem draft if any gating failures or rollout deviations occurred

Open questions / action items (owners):
- Autofallback TTL tuning — Sofia (action: run sim against 10k sessions)
- Cost-sampling heuristic edges (how to present to customers) — Aisha + Finance (action: prepare 3-line explainer)
- Confirm HSM key rotation window doesn't collide with preflight — Marcus (action: ops ticket)

Notes to self / informal:
- Watch for the 'cache-warmth paradox' — more prefill can also increase initial token cost because of repeated weight pulls; balancing act.
- Consider enabling latency-smoothing (tiny queue) for EU if spike observed in first 30m.

Runbook links and quick commands (keep short in Slack pinned):
- Revert route: /ops/tools/release revert --tag route-v1 --region all (test on staging first)
- Canary logs: k logs canary-routev2 --since 30m
- Incident template: /confluence/release/incident-template

Appendix: small deployment checklist for engineers (copy this into deployment PR):
1) Add feature flag to config and tests to verify flag behaves idempotently.
2) Ensure canary env has same weight as prod for model weight pulling.
3) Add explicit sampling keys for full payload logging (avoid PII)
4) Tag the rollout PR with JIRA: RELEASE-789

Revision history:
- 2026-05-12: initial sketch (Aisha)
- 2026-05-15: added gating thresholds and staffing matrix (Marcus)
- 2026-05-20: tightened rollback heuristics and added observability notes (Sofia)

End — keep this doc minimal and update live during rollout.
